Build More. Build Your Career.
Applications are now open for Seymour Whyte's 2027 Graduate Program, offering opportunities across Southeast Queensland, for ambitious engineering graduates looking to make an impact from day one.
Through our structured two-year development program, you'll gain hands-on experience on major civil infrastructure projects, work alongside industry leaders, receive dedicated mentoring, and develop the technical, commercial and leadership skills needed for a successful career in construction.
At Seymour Whyte you'll commence on a live project and be given meaningful responsibility from the outset, contributing to the delivery of major infrastructure projects while learning from some of the industry's most experienced professionals.
About the project
We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to commence on our Coomera Connector Stage 1 South project.
This is a significant transport infrastructure project that will improve connectivity between Logan City and the Gold Coast, providing a vital alternative to the M1 Pacific Motorway and helping to support the region's continued growth.
The project includes major earthworks, bridge construction and innovative environmental solutions, including a 300-metre bridge over the Nerang River.
Why Join Seymour Whyte?
Our Graduate Development Program combines practical project experience, formal learning, mentoring and professional development to accelerate your growth. You'll gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery, helping you build a well-rounded understanding of the civil construction industry.
- Work on landmark civil infrastructure projects
- Gain exposure to a diverse range of disciplines
- Structured graduate development and mentoring
- Build meaningful relationships with industry leaders
- Learn through real project experience
- Enjoy a supportive, collaborative and high-performing culture
- Be part of the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction and concessions
Learn From Industry Leaders
Every graduate is paired with a senior mentor who provides guidance, support and career advice throughout the program. You'll also build valuable relationships with project leaders, technical specialists and fellow graduates from across Australia.
More Than Classroom Learning
In addition to on-the-job learning, you'll participate in graduate development workshops designed to enhance your technical and professional skills, expand your industry knowledge and connect you with peers from across the business.
A Career That Keeps Moving
Supported by a structured competency framework, ongoing coaching and real project experience, you'll continually build the knowledge, confidence and capability needed to progress your career.
If you're looking for more than just a graduate job and want a career where you can learn, contribute and grow while helping deliver projects that connect communities, we'd love to hear from you.

- Assist with the management of Common Data Environments (CDEs) and digital collaboration platforms.
- Support the integration of BIM with construction planning, procurement, fabrication and installation.
- Identify opportunities to improve project delivery through digital engineering, technology and automation.

You will ideally have:
- A degree, diploma or relevant qualification in Engineering, Construction, Architecture, Building Services, Digital Engineering or a related discipline.

- Strong understanding of BIM methodologies, model coordination and information management.

James Cook University is seeking a collaborative and solutions-focused Research Engineer to join the Cyclone Testing Station in Townsville.
This is an exciting opportunity to apply your engineering expertise to research that helps reduce the social and financial impacts of tropical cyclones, thunderstorms and other severe wind events. You will contribute to practical projects examining building performance, wind loads, wind-driven debris and rain damage, while working with industry, researchers and technical specialists to strengthen community resilience.
About the role
As a Research Engineer, you will utilise your engineering expertise to engage with existing and prospective clients, develop suitable testing programs, supervise load testing activities and guide technical staff to ensure engineering best practice is achieved.
Working within the Cyclone Testing Station, you will contribute to research and testing that helps communities minimise the loss and suffering caused by cyclones and other high wind events. You will conduct and oversee testing programs, analyse data, prepare technical reports and research publications, and communicate outcomes through industry engagement, workshops and conferences.
You will also collaborate with industry partners, contribute to research informing Australian Standards, and support activities including grant applications, damage investigations and community engagement initiatives that strengthen the resilience of buildings and communities across Australia
Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
- Design and deliver testing programs aligned with relevant standards and engineering design criteria
- Apply structural analysis, laboratory testing, field investigation and probability analysis techniques
- Analyse and interpret data, preparing clear technical reports and research publications
- Collaborate with technical staff and multidisciplinary colleagues to deliver high-quality testing outcomes
- Build effective relationships with clients, industry organisations and project stakeholders
- Monitor project progress and communicate outcomes against agreed milestones
- Contribute to research supporting building resilience and relevant Australian Standards
- Support the Cyclone Testing Station’s damage investigations, grant activities and community engagement initiatives 
About you
You will bring qualifications and experience in wind, structural or mechanical engineering, or a related discipline, appropriate to appointment at Academic Level B.
You will also demonstrate:
- Contemporary knowledge of Australian Building Standards, relevant legislation and building construction techniques
- Experience delivering research projects, analysing data and communicating findings through reports or journal publications
- Strong engineering analysis, problem-solving and organisational capabilities
- The ability to manage priorities, exercise sound judgement and meet competing deadlines
- Experience engaging with industry and translating research into practical outcomes
- Excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills
- The ability to work effectively both independently and within a multidisciplinary research team
Familiarity with building systems and construction techniques, together with experience using numerical or structural analysis software, will be highly regarded. 
About the Cyclone Testing Station
The Cyclone Testing Station (CTS) is a leading research and consulting centre within James Cook University's College of Science and Engineering. CTS delivers world-class research, testing and consulting services focused on improving the resilience of buildings and communities to cyclones, thunderstorms and other severe wind events. Through collaboration with industry, government and Standards Australia, our work helps reduce the social and economic impacts of natural disasters and create safer, more resilient communities.]
Learn more about CTS on the Cyclone Testing Station website.
Why work at JCU?
Join Australia’s university for the Tropics and contribute to applied engineering research that supports safer, stronger and more resilient communities.

ABOUT US
Ertech is a proudly employee-owned Australian civil and electrical construction company, delivering high-quality services across the Transport, Infrastructure, Resources, and Defence sectors. We partner with clients in both the public and private sectors, including state and federal governments. Since our humble beginnings in 1981, we’ve built a strong reputation for the quality of our work and the long-term relationships we foster — all driven by our core values of collaboration, courage, and authenticity.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We are currently recruiting for an experienced Project Engineer to join our team in NSW, taking the lead on QA/QC requirements across our long-term construction projects. This role will involve travel between our Sydney-based project sites.
As the Project Engineer, you will play a key role in managing quality assurance and quality control activities, ensuring project requirements and standards are met. You will work closely with project teams to maintain quality processes, drive continuous improvement and embed a strong culture of quality and excellence across our projects.
Other key responsibilities include, but not limited to:
- Report to the Project Manager and client on all QA/QC matters, while managing and motivating a team of Quality Engineers
- Produce the Quality Management Plans and related Quality Management tools, including Work Packs, Inspection & Test Plans, and Check Sheets in readiness for site construction, installations and field inspections
- Ensure Project teams complete all required QA/QC surveillance and documentation to the applicable project requirements and standards
- Understand the non-conformance process and liaise with the client and the project teams to develop corrective and preventative actions to mitigate reoccurrence.
- Provide in house training to Project team members on Quality documentation and surveillance activities.
- Ensure the Contractor's and vendor's quality records and MDR's are compiled in a progressive manner throughout the course of the works
 To be successful, you will have experience and demonstrate capability in the following:
- Minimum 5+ years of relevant experience in a Quality Engineer or similar role on construction projects.
- Strong technical knowledge surrounding Civil and Electrical Engineering scopes.
- Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Bachelor in Civil Engineering or similar qualification (desirable).
- Ability to obtain a National Police Clearence.
- MUST hold relevant Australian working rights.
WHY JOIN ERTECH?
At Ertech, we’re committed to investing in our people and creating a workplace where you can thrive. Here’s what you can look forward to: 
- Competitive remuneration
- Metro-based project – enjoy the benefit of being home every night
- Full-time position offering stability and annual leave entitlements
- Supportive, team-oriented culture where collaboration and respect are valued 
- Play a key role in shaping the growth and success of our projects
- Career development and progression opportunities, annual performance development plans.
- Access to great benefits, including: 
- Discounted Private Health Insurance (HBF & Medibank)
- Annual flu vaccinations 
- Novated leasing options through Paywise
- Service recognition and milestone rewards 
- Employee Referral Program incentives

OUR CULTURE
At Ertech, our people are fundamental to our success. We're focused on creating an inclusive workplace, with the right people in the right roles, who are engaged, empowered, and appropriately rewarded. Ertech will provide you with the chance to be a part of great team, meet new people and gain experience with an industry leader who puts safety first. 
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION
We value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives of all people and actively encourage applications from First Nations peoples, all genders, culturally and linguistically diverse individuals, people with disability, LGBTQIA+ community members, and veterans of the Australian Defence Force.
Ertech is a proud Veteran Employment supporter. We recognise the valuable skills and leadership that veterans bring to our industry and welcome their applications at all levels of the business. Even if you don’t meet every requirement listed, we encourage you to apply and bring your strengths to our team.
HOW TO APPLY
Click "Apply" on this job advertisement, which will direct you to Ertech's application portal. Simply follow the steps outlined on the portal to complete your application.
This is an incredible opportunity! If you are looking for a position in an environment in which you can flourish whilst building your career, there is no better time to join the Ertech Team than now!

candidates.content_text:
Life at Fulton Hogan is about making the most of opportunities, taking responsibility, and making it happen. We appreciate our peoples' courage, curiosity and unique perspectives, and look to collaborate as much as possible to explore safer, smarter and more efficient ways of working in this rapidly changing world. We don't stand still - there are always opportunities to do more and do better.
- Keen to progress your career? Take full advantage of our tailored training, leadership, and mentoring programs; or leverage our partnerships with industry association such as Engineers Australia, the Australian Water Association, WaterAid, Chartered Accountants, CPA Australia, Infrastructure Sustainability Council, The National Association of Women in Construction, plus many more.
- Looking to enhance your wellbeing? We will encourage you to explore flexible working arrangements where possible. We offer great benefits, including corporate health and fitness programs, health insurance discounts, personal banking support, a range of retailer discounts, up to 18 weeks paid primary carers parental leave and up to 10 days paid secondary carers leave, access to our Employee Assistance Program (including your immediate family), and the option to take more time for yourself throughout the year with our Purchase Leave Policy.
- Want to help us better the communities we live and work in? Our purpose of creating, connecting, and caring for communities is more than a saying to us - it's a way of thinking, working, and living because we're locals too, and seek to give back in ways that strengthen and build resilient communities. We do this because we genuinely care, enjoy what we do, and even manage to have some fun along the way! You'll find us partnering with local and national community groups, like Clontarf Foundation, and Black Dog Institute, in addition to indigenous groups and social enterprises, to ensure that our good work positively impacts and brings about sustainable change within our industry.
- Do we offer a 'competitive' salary package? Of course! Speak to our Talent Acquisition or People & Culture team to learn more.
What's on offer?
Fulton Hogan's South East Queensland Utilities team is delivering a long term rolling program of watermain renewals as part of the Urban Utilities NG4D partnerships in Brisbane. We are seeking a Project Engineer to support the team by developing shutdown plans, and methodologies and assisting with implementation and close out in the field along with assisting the Project Manager with day‑to‑day delivery and planning.
This role suits a professional with experience in watermain renewal works and exposure to water authority networks and who enjoys detailed planning, coordination and problem solving in a fast‑paced environment.
In this role you'll be responsible for:
- Develop & provide input into detailed watermain shutdown plans for renewals, tie‑ins and cut‑ins
- Manage overall life cycle of shut planning including preparation of trial shut plans, trial shut plan close out, works delivery shutdowns and close out
- Coordinate with Urban Utilities, internal construction teams subcontractors and other stakeholders to confirm isolation points, impacts and sequencing
- Identify and mitigate risks associated with shutdowns, including customer impacts, service continuity, safety and environmental risks
- Support preparation of ITPs, SWMS and other project documentation relevant to shutdown activities
- Track and report on shutdown performance, constraints and lessons learned to improve future planning
- Help coordinate after‑hours and weekend shutdowns as required by the program.
How you'll connect to the role:
- Experience in watermain works (renewals, new mains, tie‑ins, cut‑overs or similar)
- Experience working with or for a water authority (e.g. managing water networks, shutdowns, customer impacts or maintenance activities). Experience working on Urban Utilities projects is desirable but not essential
- Strong understanding of water reticulation networks, isolation/shutdown processes and associated risks and demonstrated ability to learn quickly
- Proven ability to prepare technical documentation and methodologies with attention to detail
- Strong planning and organisational skills - able to manage multiple shutdowns and prioritising works based on importance in a rolling program environment
- Relevant qualifications in engineering is preferred but not essential, water operations or a related field are desirable but not essential - strong practical experience in water/shutdown planning is highly valued
- Adopting and driving Fulton Hogan's Living Safely 2.0 Culture.
Our people share the same set of values that keep us REAL. Respect, Energy and Effort, Attitude and Leadership encapsulate what we stand for at Fulton Hogan and encourage us to foster a diverse and inclusive culture where we listen to, care for, celebrate, and respect everyone.
We are committed to reconciliation and building and nurturing respectful relationships with First Nations peoples. Through our First Nations Engagement Strategy and Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP), we aim to promote opportunities, cultural understanding and partnerships that celebrate and acknowledge the contributions of Indigenous communities.
If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position.
For over 90 years, Fulton Hogan has been delivering high-quality infrastructure to improve the lives of people every day. Our 10,000+ team works in every kind of weather and environment, creating, connecting, and caring for communities across Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific.
